## Tours offering an optional visit to Montevideo from Buenos Aires

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is Uruguay's capital on the Río de la Plata. Its historic center begins around Independence Square and older city streets. From there, travelers can walk through Ciudad Vieja toward the port district, see early-20th-century architecture, and sample local food.

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} allowing **an optional visit** to Montevideo. In most cases, the main journey follows Argentina or several South American countries, while a visit to Uruguay can be arranged on a free day in Buenos Aires. This adds another country to the traveler's personal route but **does not make Uruguay a mandatory country on the main tour**.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_vip_tur_v_braziliyu_i_argentinu_na_10_dnej,tour_argentina_brazil_pipa_11d,tour_source_chili_i_argentina_vip}}

| Base trip | Possible addition |
|---|---|
| Brazil and Argentina | A day in Montevideo |
| Argentina and Praia de Pipa | Excursion from Buenos Aires |
| Chile and Argentina VIP | Uruguay after the main route |

## How an optional day in Montevideo works

On some itineraries, the journey begins in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and continues by ferry across the Río de la Plata. The ferry terminal, journey time, border formalities, and schedule must be coordinated for the actual dates. Planning only around a ferry departure is not enough: allow for travel to the port, boarding, document checks, and the return sailing.

After arriving in Uruguay's capital, the route may include [Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/), Palacio Salvo, the [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/), and [Montevideo Port](/uruguay/place/montevideo-port/). For a short introduction, focus on the central districts. Museums and interior visits to individual buildings depend on their hours and the confirmed program.

This format suits travelers who want to see two capitals beside one wide estuary and compare urban life in Argentina and Uruguay. One excursion day is not enough for an extended holiday on Uruguay's coast.

## Ten-day VIP tour of Brazil and Argentina

The [Brazil and Argentina VIP itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-vip-10-days/) connects Rio de Janeiro, Iguazú Falls, and Buenos Aires. Time in Argentina's capital is available for individual choices.

The program offers alternatives: a gastronomic experience, a gaucho ranch visit, or **a ferry excursion to Montevideo**. The last option includes key central sights in Uruguay, with the return to the main tour coordinated around transport and accommodation in Buenos Aires.

It would be wrong to treat all three additional experiences as simultaneously included. Montevideo replaces other free-day activities, and ferry costs and guiding arrangements must be agreed separately.

## Eleven-day itinerary through Argentina and Brazil's beaches

The [“Argentina and Brazil in 11 Days” tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-buenos-aires-el-calafate-iguazu-pipa-11-days/) begins in Buenos Aires, then continues to Patagonia's glaciers, Iguazú Falls, and finally the beaches of Praia de Pipa.

During free time in Buenos Aires, travelers can choose the Tigre area, a gaucho ranch, or **a one-day visit to Montevideo**. Unlike the main glacier-and-waterfall route, this excursion focuses on the historic center of a city.

Adding Uruguay makes the opening section busier. If you prefer a gentler start, spend the time in Buenos Aires and arrange Montevideo only if the connections work comfortably.

## Chile and Argentina VIP: Montevideo at the end

The [extended Chile and Argentina VIP itinerary](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-vip/) ends in Buenos Aires after a long journey through natural regions. In its final section, travelers may choose a visit to Tigre, a ranch, or Montevideo.

Here, Montevideo offers another capital after a prolonged nature-focused journey. Decide based on your energy for further transfers and whether you are willing to devote another day to Uruguay.

## What to see on a short Montevideo visit

A central-city route usually focuses on [Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/) and the José Artigas monument. The Citadel Gate survives near the Old Town boundary, with the recognizable Palacio Salvo nearby.

You can then walk along Ciudad Vieja's streets toward historic facades, markets, and the waterfront. [Montevideo Cathedral](/uruguay/place/montevideo-cathedral/) adds religious architecture to the city experience. Yet a brief visit is best understood as an introduction to central Montevideo rather than an overview of the whole country.

| Place | What it adds |
|---|---|
| Independence Square | National history |
| Ciudad Vieja | Historic urban center |
| Port | Río de la Plata atmosphere |

## When should you add Uruguay to a tour?

Montevideo is a worthwhile extra for travelers especially interested in South American capitals who want to use a free day to see another country. If the main priorities are glaciers, waterfalls, safari experiences, or beach relaxation, another ferry journey may simply make the trip more demanding.

Check whether you have a night in Buenos Aires before and after the excursion, the timing of the return sailing, and which documents you need to cross the border. Entry rules must be checked for your citizenship and travel dates separately from this selection.

Ada Tours can fit a Montevideo visit into a suitable route and calculate the extra service separately. Find more options in the [Uruguay tours catalog](/uruguay/tour/) and [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about an additional trip to Montevideo

### Is Montevideo included in the base price of these tours?

No. This catalog concerns an optional visit to Uruguay's capital. The sightseeing program, ferry crossing, and guiding must be agreed separately.

### Can I visit Montevideo in one day from Buenos Aires?

Some itineraries offer that option. Feasibility depends on the ferry timetable, border control, and time available for sightseeing.

### Does Montevideo have attractions besides the port?

Yes. The historic center includes Independence Square, Palacio Salvo, old neighborhoods, and museums. A short visit normally covers only part of the city.

### Does an optional excursion make the whole tour a Uruguay itinerary?

No. The principal tour countries remain unchanged. Uruguay becomes an additional country visited only if the excursion is agreed.

## Which tours include Montevideo?

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is Uruguay's capital on the Río de la Plata. Visitors can see Independence Square, Palacio Salvo, Solís Theatre, and Ciudad Vieja, then continue to the port neighborhoods or the Rambla waterfront. The city suits both a panoramic excursion and several days of gastronomy and winery visits.

**The key difference between tours through Montevideo is the capital's role in the journey.** In one program, it is the starting point for exploring Uruguay; in another, a stop between Buenos Aires and Uruguayan cities; in a third, a day trip within a much longer journey.

## Through Uruguay: the capital, wine, and coast

The [six-day “Best of Uruguay” tour](/uruguay/tour/best-of-uruguay-five-star-tour/) begins with accommodation in Montevideo. A private sightseeing excursion follows, covering Independence Square, Solís Theatre, Palacio Salvo, 18 de Julio Avenue, the Agricultural Market, and waterfront districts. A separate day is devoted to Bouza Winery and a wine-paired lunch. After the capital, travelers head to Punta del Este and visit [Punta Ballena](/uruguay/place/punta-ballena/) and [Garzón Winery](/uruguay/place/garzon-winery/).

The [“Uruguay: Wine and Old Believer Traditions” itinerary](/uruguay/tour/uruguay-wine-old-believer-traditions/) offers another perspective on Montevideo. It starts with a city tour, a traditional market, and an evening of music, then continues to Spinoglio Winery, San Javier, [Fray Bentos](/uruguay/place/fray-bentos/), and [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/). This trip appeals to people interested in migration history and cultural routes.

On the [16-day Uruguay and Paraguay tour](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/), Montevideo also opens the journey. The route then passes through Colonia, Canelones wine country, and Punta del Este, before continuing into Paraguay and the Iguazú area. Here, the capital is the first stage of a multi-country tour.

## Montevideo with Buenos Aires, Brazil, and Iguazú

The [13-day Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay trip](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) begins in Rio de Janeiro. After Iguazú Falls and Buenos Aires, travelers cross the Río de la Plata by ferry, explore Colonia, and continue to Montevideo for two nights. The city program includes the capital's main squares and attractions. This suits travelers who want to compare major cities in three countries while also visiting famous natural landmarks.

On the [20-day, six-country Latin America tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/), Montevideo is a sightseeing stop: guests take a ferry from Buenos Aires, tour the capital with a guide, and return to Argentina. The journey then continues through Chile, Bolivia, and Peru. The [32-day, eight-country tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) likewise includes a day trip to Montevideo by ferry from Buenos Aires.

For travelers, the distinction is substantial. A one-day Montevideo visit introduces the center but leaves less time for the waterfront, cuisine, and countryside excursions. Overnight stops allow the city program to be spread over several days.

## What to see depending on your available time

If you have only a few hours, focus on Independence Square, the Citadel Gate, and Ciudad Vieja. From the square, you can walk toward Solís Theatre, historic streets, and the port market. This provides an introduction through the city's history, architecture, and everyday life.

With more time, add 18 de Julio Avenue, the Legislative Palace, Rambla, and coastal districts. On wine-focused itineraries, a separate day is devoted to a winery and tasting. Select extras according to actual free hours rather than a generic list of sights.

## Comparing the itineraries

| Format | Distinctive feature |
|---|---|
| Six days in Uruguay | City, Bouza, coast |
| Four-day historical trip | Montevideo, San Javier, Anglo |
| Thirteen days, three countries | Overnight stays in Montevideo |
| Twenty to thirty-two days, several countries | Excursion from Buenos Aires |

Compare the locations of overnight stays, planned transfers, and border-crossing time. It is particularly important to distinguish a ferry to Colonia followed by a road journey to Montevideo from a direct one-day ferry excursion from Buenos Aires. These are different logistical arrangements.

Ada Tours can help choose an itinerary focused on several days in Uruguay, culture and wine, or an overview of several countries. Hotels, excursions, and included transfers follow the selected program.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Montevideo

### Can I visit Montevideo in one day from Buenos Aires?

Yes. This format appears on the [20-day six-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and the [32-day eight-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Sightseeing time depends on the ferry schedule.

### Which tours include overnight stays in Montevideo?

For example, the [six-day Uruguay itinerary](/uruguay/tour/best-of-uruguay-five-star-tour/) and the [13-day three-country journey](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) include accommodation in the capital.

### Are there winery visits near Montevideo?

Yes. The [five-star Uruguay tour](/uruguay/tour/best-of-uruguay-five-star-tour/) features Bouza, and the [wine and Old Believer traditions itinerary](/uruguay/tour/uruguay-wine-old-believer-traditions/) features Spinoglio. Tasting inclusions depend on the specific program.

### How does Montevideo differ from Colonia del Sacramento?

[Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) is known for a compact historic quarter with Portuguese and Spanish heritage. Montevideo is a much larger capital with theaters, squares, a port, museums, and a long urban waterfront.

## Piriápolis in Uruguay: a beach resort with history and hills

Piriápolis lies in Maldonado Department on the shores of the Río de la Plata. The town combines a long sandy beach, resort architecture, and hills rising close to the built-up waterfront. It is a pleasant place to spend a few quiet days or stop on the way from [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) to [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/).

What sets Piriápolis apart is the chance to combine seaside walks with hill viewpoints and buildings from the resort's early decades. Even without an organized excursion, a single day provides an introduction to its history and geography.

## Francisco Piria and the origins of the resort town

Piriápolis is associated with entrepreneur **Francisco Piria**, who purchased land in 1890 and began developing a seaside resort. Municipal historical materials record that the site was originally called *Balneario del Porvenir*.

Piria envisioned a resort with public spaces, architecture, and entertainment. Traces of that original plan survive in the center: historic buildings, avenues, fountains, and the waterfront reveal how seaside tourism developed in early-20th-century Uruguay.

One of the most notable buildings is **Argentino Hotel**, a large historic hotel near the shore. Its facade became part of the resort's recognizable appearance. You do not have to stay there to appreciate it from the surrounding streets.

## Rambla de los Argentinos and the beaches

**Rambla de los Argentinos** is the main waterfront promenade. The Piriápolis tourist association notes that it received national historic monument status in 2021. It is an enjoyable place for walking, watching the sea, and relaxing in coastal cafés.

In summer, the beach becomes the center of resort life; in cooler months, walks and views attract more attention. Water and wind conditions vary with the season, so follow local warnings and consider wave conditions before swimming.

Beyond the central beach, other coastal neighborhoods include San Francisco, Punta Fría, and Punta Colorada. The beaches differ in slope, wind exposure, and suitability for calm swimming.

## Cerro San Antonio: the town's principal panorama

**Cerro San Antonio**, a hill about 130 meters high, is one of the resort's main viewpoints. From its summit you can see the town, coastline, harbor, and nearby green hills. Religious monuments associated with Stella Maris can also be found there.

You can climb on foot or drive up. Check the operation of any other ascent facilities directly before visiting. For a walk uphill, wear non-slip shoes; rocky surfaces can be wet after rain.

On a clear day, the viewpoint makes Piriápolis' position between water and rising land easy to appreciate. It shows why the town differs from resorts built along completely flat shorelines.

## Cerro del Toro, Piria Castle, and green surroundings

There are other excursions around town. **Cerro del Toro** is known for its hilly terrain and a decorative spring with a bull figure. It is connected with the resort's early development, and walks on its slopes offer further views.

Away from the central waterfront stands **Piria Castle**, built as the founder's residence. Maldonado Municipality lists it among the town's historic attractions. Check interior access and any museum arrangements separately.

A longer outing leads to the **Cerro Pan de Azúcar** area. This is a separate nature destination, where different routes may require different fitness levels. If you are not planning a mountain hike, Cerro San Antonio and the waterfront may be enough.

## Harbor, cuisine, and resort evenings

Piriápolis has a small harbor for leisure and sailing boats. It offers a place to relax by the water and see a side of the town less focused on the central beach. Local cafés and restaurants serve fish, seafood, and familiar Uruguayan dishes.

Some waterfront venues are busier and open more consistently in high season. During quieter months, services can operate on reduced schedules. If you have special dietary needs, check individual restaurants before traveling.

## When to visit Piriápolis and how to plan a route

During the Southern Hemisphere summer, especially **December to February**, it is easier to combine sightseeing with a beach holiday. Outside the season, the town's architecture and hills invite slower exploration, weather permitting.

For one day, plan the promenade, an exterior look at Argentino Hotel, and Cerro San Antonio. If staying several days, add Cerro del Toro, the harbor, and neighboring beaches. On a longer trip, combine Piriápolis with [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) and [Punta Ballena](/uruguay/place/punta-ballena/).

Piriápolis appears among [places in Uruguay](/uruguay/place/). When selecting an operating itinerary, check the [Uruguay tours catalog](/uruguay/tour/) and its precise stops: **not every coastal itinerary includes Piriápolis**.

## Frequently asked questions about Piriápolis

### What should I see in one day?

Start with the promenade, look at the historic Argentino Hotel, and go up Cerro San Antonio. If time remains, walk near the harbor.

### Can I climb Cerro San Antonio independently?

Yes. There are pedestrian and vehicle approaches. Wear shoes with good grip for walking and account for the weather.

### Which is better for a holiday: Piriápolis or Punta del Este?

[Piriápolis](/uruguay/place/piriapolis/) suits quieter relaxation among historic buildings and green hills, whereas [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) has a livelier resort atmosphere.

### Does Piriápolis have a beach?

Yes. The central promenade follows a sandy shore, with other beach areas nearby.

### Can I visit outside summer?

Yes, for walking, architecture, and views from the hills. The swimming season depends on water temperature and actual weather.

## Punta Ballena: a coastal headland, Casapueblo, and sunset over the sea

Punta Ballena lies on the [Uruguayan](/uruguay/) coast near [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/). Rocky outcrops and broad sea views make the headland one of the best-known panoramic stops in this part of the country. But the main attraction drawing many travelers is **Casapueblo**, the unusual white building created by artist Carlos Páez Vilaró.

A visit can center on two experiences: a coastal walk and the museum. Travelers often return in the evening for sunset. The natural lookout and the specific museum program are different parts of the trip, each with its own access conditions and time requirements.

## The headland and coast: what makes the landscape special?

Punta Ballena's coast differs from the long open beaches of nearby resorts. Rocky sections, slopes, and expansive views alternate along the shore. Changing light makes a notable difference: by day, the coastline is easier to see in detail; before sunset, the sun emphasizes its silhouette.

When choosing a walking route, remember the cliffs and wind. Photographs taken at the edge can look dramatic, but marked paths and permitted viewpoints are safer. In strong winds, a brief stop near the museum may be more comfortable than a long exposed walk.

Marine mammals can be observed off Uruguay at certain times, but **the name Punta Ballena does not promise an encounter with whales**. If whale watching is the main goal, check the season, designated observation areas, and current notices from the relevant authorities separately.

## Casapueblo: an artist's house turned museum

Casapueblo is an architectural creation by Carlos Páez Vilaró, who developed his home and workshop on a seaside slope over many years. The rounded white building, terraces, and passages resemble a sculpture incorporated into the coastal landscape.

Today, it houses the artist's museum and studio. The official website describes paintings, ceramics, sculptures from different periods, a screening room, and terraces overlooking the coast. Exploring the artwork makes the museum worthwhile even on a cloudy day.

Casapueblo is best understood as a unified artistic creation. Its architecture, interiors, movement between rooms, and views over the sea were all part of the artist's vision. It is not a standard hotel or ordinary viewpoint, although the building also has other spaces.

## The sunset ceremony: what happens in the evening?

A museum tradition is the **“Ceremony of the Sun”** (*Ceremonia al Sol*). At sunset, a recording plays Carlos Páez Vilaró's voice reciting a dedication to the sun. This experience is linked to the artist's history and the atmosphere of the site.

The museum recommends arriving early, as crowds can gather at sunset. Check the official timetable and admission rules for your date: sunset times change seasonally, and weather may affect the view.

| Visiting time | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Daytime | Museum and architecture |
| Late afternoon | Terraces and coast |
| Before sunset | Ceremony of the Sun |

If your tour includes only a stop at the headland, **do not automatically assume museum admission or the ceremony is included**. Confirm these separately against the selected itinerary.

## What else can you see nearby?

Not far from Punta Ballena is the Lussich Arboretum, a wooded area with walking trails and a museum space. It is interesting for the history of its cultivated forest, botany, and birds. The arboretum's official museum project describes walks, exhibitions, and guided forest visits.

These outings offer two different landscapes: the coast and a planted forest. [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) adds beaches, restaurants, and livelier resort life. [Piriápolis](/uruguay/place/piriapolis/) can be another coastal stop on a longer itinerary.

## Including Punta Ballena in a journey

Our Uruguay itineraries include visits around Punta del Este and Casapueblo in their cultural and coastal sections. For example, [“Best of Uruguay: Five-Star Tour”](/uruguay/tour/best-of-uruguay-five-star-tour/) connects Montevideo with a journey to the coast. Confirm which stops and admissions are included in the exact version chosen before booking.

When arranging an independent visit, decide whether you would rather explore the museum in detail or watch sunset from a terrace. A short stop can make it difficult to appreciate both. Also plan transportation back after sunset.

## Frequently asked questions about Punta Ballena

### Are Punta Ballena and Punta del Este the same place?

No. Punta Ballena is a distinct coastal headland near the Punta del Este resort area. They combine easily on one trip but offer different attractions.

### What is Casapueblo?

It is an artistic building created by Carlos Páez Vilaró, housing a museum and studio with his paintings, ceramics, and sculptures. The building itself is considered an important part of his work.

### Can I visit the museum without the sunset ceremony?

Yes. The museum has exhibitions and spaces that can be explored independently of the ceremony. Check the accessibility of individual rooms and current opening times beforehand.

### Can whales be seen from the headland?

That depends on the season, the animals' location, and the weather. Encounters are not guaranteed, so plan around the coast and museum, with whale watching as a separate possibility.

## Tours through Punta Ballena: Casapueblo and sunset on Uruguay's coast

Punta Ballena is a coastal headland near the resort of Punta del Este. [Casapueblo](/uruguay/place/punta-ballena/), a white terraced building standing on the rocks and associated with artist Carlos Páez Vilaró, is located here. Travelers find a combination of museum, architecture, and sea views. It is important to establish **whether Casapueblo entry is included**, or whether an excursion merely passes through the wider Punta del Este area.

We include Punta Ballena on the [six-day “Best of Uruguay” itinerary](/uruguay/tour/best-of-uruguay-five-star-tour/). The journey combines Montevideo, the coast, Casapueblo, and two wineries. Punta Ballena is visited on a specific day as part of a private Punta del Este excursion.

## How the Punta Ballena visit works

After three nights in Montevideo, travelers move to Punta del Este and check into The Grand Hotel Punta del Este. A private afternoon excursion through the resort with an English-speaking guide then covers the yacht harbor, shopping streets, lighthouse, La Mano sculpture, city neighborhoods, and coastline.

**The final stop is Casapueblo at Punta Ballena.** Our itinerary includes museum admission, time to explore the site, and sunset with a glass of champagne. Travelers experience the artistic side of Uruguay's coast on one sightseeing day, without an additional night on the headland.

Casapueblo operates as a museum and art space dedicated to Carlos Páez Vilaró. Its position on a rocky shoreline offers coastal views. Museum hours, closing times, and sunset depend on the date, so the exact visit time is coordinated within the excursion.

## Montevideo, Punta del Este, and wineries in one tour

The six-day itinerary includes five nights: three in Montevideo and two in Punta del Este. The capital section features a city tour and a visit to Bouza Winery with a three-course wine-paired lunch. Travelers then head for the coast.

In Punta del Este, one day is devoted to the city and Punta Ballena, and another to Garzón Winery: an estate visit and a seasonal four-course lunch paired with wine. At the end, a private transfer takes guests to Montevideo airport or port.

| Day | Program |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | Montevideo, city tour, Bouza |
| 4 | Punta del Este, Casapueblo, Punta Ballena |
| 5 | Garzón Winery and gastronomic lunch |
| 6 | Return transfer to Montevideo |

The route combines urban life, artistic heritage, coastal panoramas, and tastings. It does not list extended nature hikes on Punta Ballena, yacht cruises, or whale watching among included services.

## What to check when choosing this tour

The key question is **what kind of stop at the headland is included**. In this itinerary, entry to Casapueblo is included as part of the day spent exploring Punta del Este. Hotel location matters as well: guests stay two nights at the resort itself, so Punta Ballena does not require a long round trip from the capital.

For comparison, see the [Punta Ballena destination page](/uruguay/place/punta-ballena/) and the [full six-day itinerary](/uruguay/tour/best-of-uruguay-five-star-tour/). The selection covers {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Take the number of nights, stops, included transfers, and excursions from the actual itinerary rather than a general description of the coast.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Punta Ballena

### Is Casapueblo admission included?

Yes. The six-day Ada Tours itinerary explicitly lists the private Punta del Este excursion and admission to Casapueblo.

### Do I need an overnight stay at Punta Ballena?

The itinerary includes two nights in Punta del Este, not a separate overnight stay at the headland. Punta Ballena is visited during an excursion day.

### Can I watch sunset at Casapueblo?

The program includes a sunset visit with a glass of champagne. The precise timing depends on your travel date and the museum's hours.

### Is this mainly a beach holiday?

The itinerary combines city sightseeing, two wineries, art, and a coastal resort. Beach relaxation is possible at Punta del Este, but no extended dedicated beach days are scheduled in this six-day program.
